content.comment_body: Good day, I would greatly appreciate your assistance. On the [product_name], 400 V was mistakenly applied instead of 220 V, which resulted in the device being damaged. I replaced the input varistor and capacitor, and the other components seem to be intact based on my inspection. When powered at 220 V, the screen does not respond. I have already purchased a new unit, but I need to temporarily activate the damaged one to recover its program since we do not have a backup. Thank you very much for any help. [user_name]

Hello [user_name], Please post your question in English, as this is an international community and responses will be easier to generate in one common language. Below is the translation of your post (via Google Translate): Kind regards, [user_name]

Good morning, I would really appreciate your help. On the [product_name], 400 V was accidentally used instead of 220 V, leading to device failure. I have replaced the input varistor and capacitor, and the remaining parts appear to be functional. I checked them. After reconnecting to 220 V, the display does not respond. Although I have procured a replacement, it is crucial to get the damaged unit operational to extract the program, as no backup is available. Thanks a lot for your support. [user_name]
Unfortunately, no forum members will be able to help. The [product_name] appears to be permanently damaged.
Hi, have you tried pinging the [product_name] or connecting with [product_name] software? If these attempts have failed, the device is most likely destroyed. Best regards.
There's no possibility to recover it! Greetings, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user experienced fatal failure of a [product_name] after applying incorrect voltage. Despite replacing some components, the device remains nonfunctional and cannot be accessed to retrieve the essential program. Responses from other community members confirm the damage is irreversible, and no recovery solutions are available.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to temporarily restore the malfunctioning [product_name] to recover the program stored within, since no backup exists.
